newsitem.title: USA: London Fog to close rainwear plant in Baltimore.
newsitem.headline: London Fog to close rainwear plant in Baltimore.

text.p: London Fog Industries Inc. said Wednesday it will close its rainwear sewing plant in Park Circle Industrial Park in Baltimore, Md., as of June 6.
The plant, which employs 281 people, was closed in October 1994 and re-opened in January 1995 in cooperation with the city and Maryland as well as the plant's employee union.

The company said the reopening was part of an experiment to determine whether a domestic rainwear manufacturing facility could provide quick response to retail inventory demand and compete with off-shore contractors.
London Fog, one of the country's largest manufacturers of formal rainwear and outerwear, said the experiment was too costly to continue.

The company said it has a programme to help the plant's employees find new jobs. It will offer part-time jobs during peak periods at its Eldersburg, Md., facility over four months beginning in July to at least 30 employees from the Baltimore plant.

London Fog, a privately held company based in Eldersburg, also has offices in New York City and operates 120 factory outlet direct retail stores across the United States and in Puerto Rico. It has more than 1,600 employees.
